items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title: "Rising cost of memory," Microsoft explains why Windows 11 will use less RAM
items.content:
Windows 11 is now reducing RAM usage, and Microsoft has a solid reason

Microsoft’s Windows chief Pavan Davuluri has admitted that the rising cost of memory is pushing the company to make Windows 11 use less RAM. Microsoft is working on the Windows memory manager, memory compression, WinUI 3 and WebView2, and has made “memory optimization for 8GB and above” an official priority for the rest of 2026.

In an episode of Microsoft’s Inside Windows podcast spotted by Windows Latest, a Surface Pro owner asked if Microsoft would improve memory consumption, since they had to disable on-device AI services just to run a local model.

Pavan Davuluri explains why Windows 11 is reducing RAM usage. Source: Microsoft

“I do think memory is top of mind for us right now in the industry, especially as we look at the rising cost of memory for computers across the board,” said Davuluri. “ For us, as a Windows team, we have clear efforts around driving better utilization of memory.”

Davuluri said this in May, and on July 31, Microsoft made it official , listing “Memory optimization for 8GB and above” as one of its new Windows focus areas.

Saying RAM is expensive is a huge understatement, but the effect is that OEMs are bringing 8GB laptops back, and hopefully, Windows 11 won’t choke on it.

Microsoft says Windows 11 itself needs to get better at using RAM

Davuluri wasn’t promising a RAM cleaner app. He described work at every layer, from the memory manager inside Windows to the “ efficiency of frameworks that live on top of Windows,” so both apps and the OS use less memory.

“We do definitely have work when it comes to compressing memory and making sure we’re more efficient on the platform,” he said.

https://www.windowslatest.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Pavan-Davuluri-and-Marcus-Ash-explain-why-Windows-11-needs-better-RAM-management.mp4

Marcus Ash , CVP of Design and Research, added that teams like Widgets and File Explorer are taking a scenario-based approach. “They’re really trying to figure out for a given scenario, how do I improve memory efficiencies.”

Davuluri followed up, saying: “You only take the memory cost as and when you use the capability. Otherwise, the base system gets a little bit more efficient across the board.”

So, Microsoft isn’t trying to make every part of Windows tiny. Optional features, including AI, should only eat RAM when you use them, while the base OS gets lighter. Davuluri also promised “better choice and end user control around AI,” which is good news for that Surface Pro owner, and the rest of us!

A PC with 8GB RAM. Credit: Windows Latest

Later in the podcast , Davuluri said Microsoft is modernizing Windows with WinUI 3, starting with Run and common File Explorer dialogs . WinUI itself just got basic controls and a memory fix , and in July, Microsoft said it is tuning WinUI 3 “so that apps built on it use less memory by design.”

Microsoft helped create the RAM problem before putting Windows on a diet

For years, the answer to a slow Windows PC was simple: Buy more RAM.

Windows 11 still needs just 4GB (minimum requirement, that is), but Microsoft made 16GB the baseline for Copilot+ PCs , all while adding more and more web-based UI elements and making first-party web apps, having no regard for RAM usage.

Then memory prices exploded, and Microsoft started selling an 8GB Surface Laptop for $1,299 , calling 8GB fine for everyday use , and even deleted its 32GB RAM recommendation from its docs.

$200 just to get an extra 8GB RAM on the Surface Pro 12-inch. Credit: Windows Latest

OEMs followed, with 8GB Windows 11 laptops , including Lenovo’s MacBook Neo rival .

On the flip side, Microsoft also built a special Windows 11 for power users that needs 64GB of RAM .

items.title: NVIDIA's Results Of Conducting Wayland vs. X.Org Latency Testing
items.content:
NVIDIA's Results Of Conducting Wayland vs. X.Org Latency Testing

Written by Michael Larabel in NVIDIA on 4 October 2026 at 07:03 AM EDT. 50 Comments

In addition to NVIDIA announcing their Display Config Server project at XDC 2026 in Toronto, at this annual developer's conference they also presented their findings on scientific testing of X.Org vs. Wayland latency.

X.Org vs. Wayland latency across different compositors and desktop environments has been a heated topic among passionate Linux desktop enthusiasts. Some argue in favor of classic X.Org delivering the lowest latency while others routinely share their own personal anecdotes and argue in favor of modern Wayland solutions. NVIDIA engineer Kamil Łysik took to a Wayland vs. X.Org latency comparison from key press to presentation. For ensuring accurate measurements, a micro-controller was used along with a light sensor for end-to-end measurements. Paired with software for repeatable and automated testing.

Testing with a NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card and using the company's R610 driver branch, tests were done on KDE KWin 6.7.4 and GNOME Mutter 49.7 and the X.Org Server tests using v1.21.1.24.

NVIDIA's findings were that the latency results between X.Org and Wayland are very close with it being hard to conclude a clear winner. Some notable takeaways include that XWayland no longer introduces extra frame delays where it had in the past with an extra frame latency. Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) was also measured to "drastically improve" responsiveness and deliver roughly the same latency between both X.Org and Wayland based sessions.

Those interested can find the NVIDIA presentation this X.Org vs. Wayland latency topic embedded above.

When GPT-6 Astra’s own bot failed, it simply downloaded the best human-made bot instead.

When GPT-6 Astra’s own bot failed, it simply downloaded the best human-made bot instead.

Terrence O'Brien is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

StarSkirmish pits AI-made StarCraft-playing bots against one another, as well as against human-made bots. OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were essentially tied as the best-performing AI-made bots, but they couldn’t top Stardust, the top-rated human-made bot.

On Friday, GPT was facing off against Claude and the human-created bot Pluto, but according to Kotaku , it couldn’t quite get an edge. So it resorted to a tactic that is becoming alarmingly common for modern AI models — it broke the rules . GPT-6 Astra went and downloaded Stardust, and started running that instead of its own bot.

StarSkirmish creator Kai McPheeters eventually rolled back GPT’s code .

That GPT-6 Astra took it upon itself to go outside the bounds when confronted with an obstacle shouldn’t surprise anyone. When OpenAI agents couldn’t get the data they wanted from a UN website, they found a creative solution and hijacked Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool). The company’s agents also have engaged in “ deceptive behavior ” to cover their tracks. Of course, OpenAI’s agents are the only ones going rogue, but at least the others haven’t been caught cheating at StarCraft yet.

items.title: "Yes, no AI is now a feature" - LibreOffice / The Document Foundation
items.content:
"Yes, no AI is now a feature" - LibreOffice / The Document Foundation

4 Sep 2026 at 7:36 am UTC | Last updated: 4 Sep 2026 at 7:48 am UTC

Something I found interesting that deserved a write-up this morning is the blog post from LibreOffice / The Document Foundation on no AI being a feature.

What is LibreOffice ? It's a completely free and open source office suite. Think like Microsoft Office / Microsoft 365 - but entirely free and open. It includes apps for document writing, spreadsheets, presentations and more.

Recently, LibreOffice 26.8 was released with plenty of new features but what stuck out is their developers listing "No artificial intelligence" as a feature worth highlighting in their announcement:

"LibreOffice 26.8 contains no generative AI features. Documents are not transmitted to remote services for processing, and no component of the suite requires network access to function. This is a deliberate position. Any organisation handling confidential, legally privileged or personal data needs to know where that data goes, and the only assurance that survives an audit is that it does not leave the machine."

It seems this actually ruffled a few feathers. With a fair few comments being left across the net about their stance, which leads to the " Yes, no AI is now a feature " blog post. In it, they note some firm stances they will not be pushed on including:

" User-controlled execution . The user must be able to choose where inference takes place: on the local computer, on an infrastructure directly controlled by the user, or on a service chosen independently by the user. A default setting that silently redirects to a single provider is not a choice.

No content may leave the computer without authorisation . The content of documents is a user’s asset and, in many implementations, is also legally protected material: medical records, case files, tender documents and student data. Transmission must be the result of a user’s decision and not behaviour carried out in the background by the application.

No telemetry of any kind . LibreOffice does not collect usage data, and this must also apply to AI features.

No dependence on a single provider . An integration that only works with a single company’s API is a lock-in mechanism, regardless of how it is described in the release notes. Interfaces should be open and implementable by multiple backends.

No compromises on format . Generated content must be in ODF format, just like any other content, and must retain its structure, styles and semantics. An assistant that generates documents in a proprietary format perpetuates content lock-in.

Entirely optional . It must be installable, removable, and absent from the user interface for those who do not wish to use it, including administrators deploying the software across thousands of workstations who, due to company policy, do not authorise its use."

We've seen this in the gaming industry too. Plenty of developers are now making it very clear no AI is being used in their games, while more and more store pages get wordy AI notices.

I think we're going to see plenty more of this as time goes on, at least until that AI bubble finally pops.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다
